'''Katherine J. Franz''' (born 1972) is an American chemist. She is the chair of the department of chemistry at [[Duke University]]. She studies metal ion coordination in biological systems and looks to use the insight to manage species such as copper and iron. Franz was awarded the [[American Chemical Society]] ''Award for Encouraging Women into Careers in the Chemical Sciences.''

== Early life and education ==
Born 1972, Franz studied at [[Wellesley College]] and earned her bachelor's degree in 1995.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://sites.duke.edu/franzlab/people/|title=People – The Franz Lab|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> She was a member of the [[Wellesley College]] cross country team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newmac.prestosports.com/sports/wxc/history/AllC/awards1994|title=NEWMAC|website=NEWMAC|language=en|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> She moved to [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for her graduate studies, where she worked under the supervision of [[Stephen J. Lippard]] and completed her PhD in 2001.<ref name=":0" /> Her research considered the nitric oxide reactivity of [[manganese]], iron and cobalt [[tropocoronand ligand]]s.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Nitric oxide reactivity of manganese, iron and cobalt tropocoronands and development of fluorescent aminotroponiminates for nitric oxide sensing|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|date=2000|degree=Thesis|first=Katherine J. (Katherine Jennings)|last=Franz|hdl=1721.1/29590|hdl-access=free}}</ref> She was an [[National Institutes of Health]] postdoctoral fellow from 2000 to 2003.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
Franz became an assistant professor at [[Duke University]] in 2003.<ref name=":0" /> She is an Associate member of the Duke Cancer Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dukecancerinstitute.org/member/franz-katherine-j|title=Franz, Katherine J.|date=2016-12-20|website=Duke Cancer Institute|access-date=2019-08-27}}{{Dead link|date=April 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2005, Franz was awarded an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]]. She was made a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] in 2008 and promoted to professor in 2015.<ref name=":0" />

Franz has investigated the use of cellular metals in [[antimicrobial resistance]]. For example, by disrupting the amount of iron in a cell it is possible to withhold an essential pathogen, limiting the growth of microbes. On the other hand, copper can be used to control the growth of microbes, and immune cells appear to move copper to kill pathogens. At the same time, pathogens try to use copper to enhance their resistance and likelihood of survival. Franz attempts to use copper in the same way as biological systems to target [[antimicrobial]] agents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.umbc.edu/dr-katherine-j-franz/|title=Dr. Katherine J. Franz - Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry - UMBC|website=chemistry.umbc.edu|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> She has looked at iron and copper as [[ionophore]]s; which are important in the virulence of ''[[Cryptococcus neoformans]]''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://sites.duke.edu/franzlab/research/|title=Research – The Franz Lab|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref>

Franz also works on anti-cancer prochelators; molecules that do not have much affinity for metal ions, but can be triggered until they undergo a chemical conversion. Cancer cells have different [[metallome]]s than normal cells. For example, [[prostate cancer]] results in the overexpression of copper trafficking proteins, causing a high level of copper. She looks to target these copper ions by creating prochelators that become activated in the microenvironment of cancer.<ref name=":1" /> [[Gamma-glutamyltransferase]] is an enzyme that is overexpressed in cancer, and releases the [[Chelation|chelator]] [[dithiocarbamate]] from the prochelator developed by Franz's research group, which forms a toxic copper complex.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Bakthavatsalam S, Sleeper ML, Dharani A, George DJ, Zhang T, Franz KJ | title = Leveraging γ-Glutamyl Transferase To Direct Cytotoxicity of Copper Dithiocarbamates against Prostate Cancer Cells | journal = Angewandte Chemie | volume = 57 | issue = 39 | pages = 12780–12784 | date = September 2018 | pmid = 30025197 | pmc = 6372289 | doi = 10.1002/anie.201807582 }}</ref> She works on iron chelators that can be used to remove deleterious iron in brain regions impacted by [[Parkinson's disease]] without damaging the healthy metal ions. The chelators developed by Franz have no affinity for iron until a mask is released by [[hydrogen peroxide]], releasing a [[reactive oxygen species]] that combines with [[iron]] to form [[hydroxyl radicals]].<ref name=":1" /> Additionally Franz studies copper-binding peptides such as [[histatin]]. Histatin binds to copper ''in vitro'', but it is not clear how they interact or how the anti-fungal activity is modified. The Franz group have studied the anti-fungal activity of [[Histatin|Histatin-5]] against ''[[Candida albicans]]''.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Conklin SE, Bridgman EC, Su Q, Riggs-Gelasco P, Haas KL, Franz KJ | title = Specific Histidine Residues Confer Histatin Peptides with Copper-Dependent Activity against Candida albicans | journal = Biochemistry | volume = 56 | issue = 32 | pages = 4244–4255 | date = August 2017 | pmid = 28763199 | pmc = 5937946 | doi = 10.1021/acs.biochem.7b00348 }}</ref>

=== Academic service ===
Alongside her academic research, Franz is committed to mentoring early career researchers.<ref>{{Citation|title=Having Multiple Mentors: Katherine J. Franz| date=18 March 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j2Mc_5YGop8&list=PLFBRaRiWUlGpcptL13ymyVNu0ItaP7zqI|language=en|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Duke University]] Dean's Award for Excellence in Mentoring in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gradschool.duke.edu/about/news/katherine-j-franz-2016-dean-s-award-winner|title=Katherine J. Franz, 2016 Dean's Award Winner {{!}} Duke Graduate School|website=gradschool.duke.edu|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> In 2019 Franz was awarded the [[American Chemical Society]] ''Award for Encouraging Women into Careers in the Chemical Sciences.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cen.acs.org/acs-news/programs/ACS-2020-national-award-winners/97/i33|title=ACS 2020 national award winners|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref>

Franz co-edited the [[American Chemical Society]] ''Metals in Medicine [[Chemical Reviews]].''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/toc/chreay/119/2|title=Chemical Reviews {{!}} Vol 119, No 2|website=pubs.acs.org|language=en|access-date=2019-08-27}}</ref> Franz was made the chair of the [[Gordon Research Conferences|Gordon Research Conference]] on Metals in Medicine in 2013.
